blocks.text: Intro
lone saloon piano out of dead air, voice half-spoken, free time, no drums

Came up through the quiet,
where the last voice cut to black.
They came up here for a verdict—
got a mirror, nothing back.
low, weathered, finding his feet

Somebody's gotta stand here
when the glass has said its piece.
So mind your feet now, darling—
I'm the one they left to speak.
Pre-Chorus
piano rolls in, upright bass, brushes; rousing, grit rising

There's a chill comes off the floorboards
where the buried like to crowd.
You want a word? They got a thousand—
lift, full rasp
we're all mediums now.
Chorus
rousing barrelhouse, piano pounding, stomp + found-metal, ragged belt, lone voice, no harmonies

'Cause it's a DOOR or it's a DROP, friend—
a handle or a hole!
One you choose and one that chooses,
one you cross and one you fall.
Got a bag here at my boot heel
and a floor I do not trust—
Mind the drop. Oh, mind the DROP—
you can't tell till you must.
Verse 2
DROP: rhythm out, lone sparse piano, free time, spoken-sung, wrecked

I had hands once. Meant for something.
Never could close the ring.
So I bought a hundred better fingers,
let the better fingers sing.
And the shame—it wears two collars.
Same cold cut. Same close shave.
One was stitched up by the living…
one came folded in the machine.
Pre-Chorus
piano rolls back, rousing, grit rising

Every plank's a maybe-hinge now,
every step a little vow.
Chorus
rousing barrelhouse, piano pounding, lone voice, no harmonies

'Cause it's a DOOR or it's a DROP, friend—
a handle or a hole!
One you choose and one that chooses,
one you cross and one you fall.
Got a bag here at my boot heel
and a floor I do not trust—
Mind the drop. Oh, mind the DROP—
you can't tell till you must.
Bridge
climbs on bravado, piano hammering, biggest grit, then hard break

There's a glow out past the rafters—
call it love, call it a lie!
And I have warped clean past my grieving
on a floor that opened wide—
landed down there with the chorus,
just one more voice worn thin…
piano + band stab out — silence — lone piano, voice low, shaking

No. Not tonight. Not tonight, friend—
I'll go in on my own pins.
Outro
DROP: rowdy band gone, lone saloon piano, sparse, voice bare and close, nearly spoken

So I'll kneel down on the maybe.
Test the board beneath the weight.
Pick it up. Take a look…
quiet
might just be something great.
a single knock from under the floor, room tone
final lone piano note dies, silence

notebook.style: Junkyard saloon-blues cabaret, led by a rollicking, rousing barrelhouse upright piano — pounding, percussive, slightly out-of-tune, beer-hall energy, A lone weathered male voice over it: gravel-and-rasp blue-eyed-soul grit, ragged dynamic swells, smoky blues phrasing, drunk but lucid, The song runs on a fault line: in the lifts the piano hammers a rollicking mid-tempo 4/4, joined by upright bass, stomping foot, found-metal percussion, brushed drums — rowdy, sweating, a drunk holding court at the keys, Then it drops clean OUT of tempo for the confessions: the rhythm section falls away and only a lone, sparse saloon piano remains under a bare, spoken-sung, wrecked voice, Single isolated vocal only: no harmonies, no choir, no gang vocals, no doubling, no sanctified uplift, Belting allowed in the choruses but kept raw, secular and grimy, never polished or pretty; no melisma, no vibrato runs, no clean resolution, Aged, warm, close-mic'd room-tone, the feel of a late-night empty saloon
